First, let's draw a sketch of our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/4f4e38950d36bf77ce4b2a907f07b3f9c4b40837729ef644f37ecfbd921aec8a.png)

  

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/b8075ab5905ada88b2a198f73738b2c0c507371cfea32b560c02be4f0185c92f.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,-x-1\le y\le x+1\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,x-1\le y\le -x+1\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{|x|+|y|\le 1}{e}^{x+y}\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}{e}^{x+y}\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}{e}^{x+y}\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{-x-1}^{x+1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x-1}^{-x+1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[{e}^{x+y}]_{-x-1}^{x+1}\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}[{e}^{x+y}]_{x-1}^{-x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({e}^{2x+1}-{e}^{-1})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}(e-{e}^{2x-1})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{e}^{2x+1}}{2}-{e}^{-1}x]}_{-1}^{0}+{[ex-\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{e}{2}-(\frac{{e}^{-1}}{2}+{e}^{-1})]+[(e-\frac{e}{2})+\frac{{e}^{-1}}{2}] \\  & =e-{e}^{-1}.\end{aligned}
$$
